summary: This Standards Track document specifies BGP encodings and procedures for P2MP trees and Ingress Replication used in BGP/MPLS IP VPNs and EVPNs in a Segment Routing domain. It updates RFC 6514 and RFC 7988.

plainLanguage.summary: Multicast VPN and Ethernet VPN carry one customer's broadcast or multicast traffic across a provider network. This RFC adds two ways to build that transport over a network that uses Segment Routing: a branching tree computed by a controller, or a separate copy sent to each site.

questions: evpn ingress replication over segment routing
subtitle: How BGP advertises Segment Routing multicast trees and ingress replication for multicast and Ethernet VPNs.

tldr.problem: Multicast VPN and Ethernet VPN providers need to carry customer multicast and broadcast traffic across a Segment Routing network, either over a tree built by a controller or by sending separate unicast copies to each destination.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two new PMSI tunnel types for SR-MPLS and SRv6 point-to-multipoint trees, three new SRv6 endpoint behaviors, and BGP auto-discovery procedures that tie a tree's leaf set to the VPN routes. It also adds a Color Extended Community so ingress replication can carry a service level agreement.
tldr.outcome: The procedures are usable in both SR-MPLS and SRv6 data planes. The RFC updates RFC 6514 and RFC 7988 and asks IANA for two tunnel types and three SRv6 endpoint behaviors.

today: RFC 10018 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2026. It updates RFC 6514 and RFC 7988, and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Scope of the Document
sections.content:
RFC 6513 and RFC 6514 specify how a network operator provides Multicast VPN (MVPN) service. Customer multicast traffic is tunneled across the provider network over Provider Tunnels, or P-tunnels. A P-tunnel can be instantiated using different transport mechanisms.

In a provider network that uses Segment Routing (SR), a P-tunnel can be an SR Point-to-Multipoint tree defined by an SR P2MP Policy (RFC 9960), or it can use SR P2MP Ingress Replication (IR). This document calls a P-tunnel realized by an SR P2MP Policy an SR P2MP P-tunnel. These P-tunnels can be instantiated for both Segment Routing over MPLS (SR-MPLS, RFC 8660) and Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6, RFC 8986).

The RFC extends the BGP auto-discovery procedures of RFC 6514 for P-tunnels built with a P2MP tree instance, and extends RFC 7988 for IR with a Service Level Agreement (SLA). It also defines new SRv6 Endpoint behaviors used for both. For BGP MPLS-Based Ethernet VPN (RFC 7432, updated by RFC 9572), P-tunnels are advertised for handling multi-destination traffic and can be instantiated by SR-MPLS or SRv6 P2MP trees.

The RFC states that use of PIM for auto-discovery and support for customer BIDIR-PIM are outside its scope, and that the reader is expected to be familiar with RFC 6513 and RFC 6514 for MVPN procedures and with RFC 7432 for EVPN procedures.
sections.plainLanguage: Multicast VPN and Ethernet VPN carry one customer's broadcast or multicast traffic across a provider network. This RFC adds two ways to build that transport over a network that uses Segment Routing: a branching tree computed by a controller, or a separate copy sent to each site.

sections.title: The SR P2MP P-Tunnel
sections.content:
A Provider Edge (PE) router can steer customer traffic into a P-tunnel realized by an SR-MPLS or SRv6 P2MP tree instance. The tree instance is instantiated by a candidate path of an SR P2MP Policy, and the P-tunnel is signaled in MVPN or EVPN auto-discovery routes using the BGP PMSI Tunnel Attribute (PTA), which identifies the P-tunnel used to instantiate a PMSI.

On the ingress PE, a conceptual MVPN or EVPN module interacts with an SR P2MP Policy module, as shown in Figure 1 of the RFC. That module creates and updates the policy, the candidate path and the leaf set, and signals them to a controller using protocols such as PCEP, BGP or NETCONF, which are outside the scope of this document. The controller computes the tree and instantiates the tree instance on the nodes that are part of it by stitching Replication segments (RFC 9524) at the Root node, the intermediate replication nodes and the Leaf nodes.

The Tree-SID is the unique data plane identifier of the tree instance. The Root node encapsulates the payload in the Tree-SID to steer it into the tree. The provider routers replicate the encapsulated payload using Replication segments towards the Leaf nodes, and the Leaf nodes dispose of the Tree-SID and deliver the payload. A Leaf node derives the MVPN or EVPN instance for delivering the payload from either the Tree-SID or another context encoded in the packet.

An ingress PE creates a candidate path of an SR P2MP Policy when the MVPN or EVPN module is provisioned for the SR P2MP P-tunnel, or when policy maps a flow to a new P-tunnel. It deletes the candidate path when the P-tunnel is no longer required. An egress PE associates an MVPN or EVPN auto-discovery route with an MVPN or EVPN context and asks the SR P2MP Policy module to join the P-tunnel as a Leaf or a Bud node.

With Ingress Replication, the ingress PE delivers the payload to each egress PE itself. The SR P2MP Policy module and the controller take no part in it.
sections.plainLanguage: A tree has one Root that sends the traffic and several Leaf nodes that receive it. Provider routers in the middle copy the packet at each branch point. The Root labels the packet with a Tree-SID, which is the number every router in the tree uses to find the next copy.

sections.title: The PMSI Tunnel Attribute for SR P2MP Trees
sections.content:
A PTA for an SR P2MP P-tunnel carries one of two new Tunnel Types from the PMSI Tunnel Types registry: 0x0C for an SR-MPLS P2MP Tree and 0x0D for an SRv6 P2MP Tree. The Tunnel Identifier is the pair <Root, Tree-ID> from RFC 9960, encoded in that exact order. The Tree-ID is a 32-bit unsigned value that uniquely identifies an SR P2MP Policy at the Root, and the Root is an IPv4 or IPv6 address whose type can be inferred from the length of the attribute. An implementation SHOULD advertise such an attribute only when the underlying data plane is supported.

When an SR P2MP P-tunnel is not shared across MVPNs, so that there is a one-to-one association between an MVPN instance and the P-tunnel, the MPLS Label field is set to zero and the Tree-SID is enough to identify the MVPN instance. RFC 6514 also allows a PE to aggregate two or more MVPNs onto one SR P2MP P-tunnel. In that case the MPLS Label field carries a context bound to a specific MVPN instance.

In SR-MPLS, the label MUST be an upstream-assigned MPLS label (RFC 5331) or one from a global context such as the Domain-wide Common Block (RFC 9573), bound by the advertising PE to the MVPN. The ingress PE MUST impose this label before the label representing the Tree-SID. The RFC names the trade-off: sharing one P-tunnel across MVPNs means two MPLS labels have to be imposed on ingress and disposed on egress.

In SRv6, the label field carries an upstream-assigned SRv6 Multicast Service SID bound to the MVPN, or one from a global context. When the Transposition Scheme of encoding from RFC 9252 is used, the high-order 20 bits of the MPLS Label field carry the whole or a portion of the Function part of the SID, and the Transposition Length MUST be less than or equal to 20 and less than or equal to the Function Length. When the scheme is not used, the label field MUST be zero and the Transposition Length MUST be zero.

The advertising ingress PE MUST attach a BGP Prefix-SID attribute (RFC 8669) to the relevant auto-discovery routes with the SRv6 L3 Service TLV to signal the SID. The Root MUST encapsulate the payload in an outer IPv6 header with a Segment Routing Header in which the SRv6 Multicast Service SID is the last segment in the segment list. An egress PE MUST NOT install that SID in its forwarding table, because the SID is not significant on the ingress PE.
sections.plainLanguage: Each router advertises the tree in BGP with a PMSI Tunnel Attribute. The attribute names the tunnel type, 0x0C for SR-MPLS or 0x0D for SRv6, and identifies the tree by the pair of its Root address and its Tree-ID, a 32-bit number.

sections.title: Auto-Discovery Procedures
sections.content:
A PE interacts with its SR P2MP Policy module to create a candidate path, with optional traffic engineering constraints and an optional optimization objective, when it originates an Intra-AS I-PMSI auto-discovery route, an Inter-AS I-PMSI auto-discovery route for an intra-AS segment, an S-PMSI auto-discovery route, or a wildcard S-PMSI auto-discovery route (RFC 6625) whose PTA has an SR P2MP P-tunnel type. The candidate path is deleted when the PE withdraws the route advertising that P-tunnel. When a PE originates an Inter-AS I-PMSI or an S-PMSI auto-discovery route with such a PTA, it MUST set the Leaf Information Required flag.

An ingress PE discovers a Leaf node when it imports an Intra-AS I-PMSI auto-discovery route or a Leaf A-D route from an egress PE, and it adds that egress PE as a Leaf node in the SR P2MP Policy module. It removes the egress PE from the Leaf set when that route is withdrawn.

An egress PE asks to join the SR P2MP Policy as a Leaf or Bud node when it imports an Intra-AS I-PMSI, Inter-AS I-PMSI or S-PMSI auto-discovery route from an ingress PE whose PTA has an SR P2MP P-tunnel type. The egress PE MUST originate a Leaf A-D route if the Leaf Information Required flag is set in the PTA, and MUST withdraw that route when the ingress PE withdraws its route.

The EVPN procedures in Section 4.1.3 follow the same pattern with different routes. The IMET route plays the part of the Intra-AS I-PMSI route, and the S-PMSI and Leaf A-D routes of RFC 9572 are analogous to their MVPN counterparts. A PE creates the candidate path when it originates an IMET or S-PMSI auto-discovery route, and MUST set the Leaf Information Required flag on an S-PMSI route with an SR P2MP PTA.
sections.plainLanguage: An egress router signals that it wants to receive the traffic by advertising a route back to the ingress router. The ingress router adds it to the leaf set of the policy and tells the controller, which recomputes the tree.

sections.title: Ingress Replication with a Service Level Agreement
sections.content:
With Ingress Replication, the payload is encapsulated in SR-MPLS or SRv6 at the ingress PE and replicated, with each copy sent to an egress PE by unicast. RFC 7988 specifies procedures that can be reused to give MVPN service with IR in an SR domain, providing best-effort unicast connectivity. This RFC adds procedures for an MVPN IR service with an SLA from an ingress PE to an egress PE, for both SR-MPLS and SRv6, and new procedures for MVPN IR over SRv6 with or without an SLA.

The mechanism is the Color Extended Community (RFC 9012) with the Color-Only Type extension from RFC 9830, carried in BGP Update messages for AFI/SAFI 1/129 (MVPN-IPv4) and 2/129 (MVPN-IPv6). An egress PE colors its Leaf or Intra-AS I-PMSI auto-discovery route. The ingress PE then replicates the customer payload to that egress PE by steering it into the matching SR-TE policy (RFC 9256), encapsulating the payload into the segment list of that policy along with the IR MPLS label or SRv6 Multicast Service SID received from the egress PE.

The RFC gives the SR-MPLS case in numbers. Egress PE2 sends a Leaf A-D route with Color Extended Community C1 with Color-Only Type 0 and IR label L10 to ingress PE1. The segment list of the SR-TE policy (C1, PE2) at PE1 is <L1, L2, L3>. PE1 then encapsulates the MVPN payload into the MPLS label stack <L1, L2, L3, L10>, with L10 as the Bottom-of-Stack label.

For SRv6, the egress PE attaches a Prefix-SID attribute carrying an SRv6 Multicast Service SID, which MUST be routable within its AS, and the ingress PE puts it into the Segment Routing Header. The RFC gives the SRv6 case as PE1 encapsulating the payload into an IPv6 header with SRH (PE1, S1) (S10, S3, S2; SL=3) (payload).

The Color Extended Community is not used with an SR P2MP P-tunnel. The RFC explains why: packets are replicated inside the tree instance, so it is not possible to have a different traffic engineering treatment towards each egress PE. For a tree, the ingress PE dictates the treatment by setting the constraints and the metric optimization in the candidate path of the policy.
sections.plainLanguage: With ingress replication the sender makes one copy per destination and sends each as a unicast packet. This RFC adds a way for each receiver to ask for a specific service level: the receiver puts a color value on its route, and the sender steers that copy into the traffic engineering policy with the matching color.

sections.title: EVPN Specifics and Split-Horizon Filtering
sections.content:
For EVPN, the PTA is constructed as in the MVPN case, except for the MPLS Label and Flags fields. In SR-MPLS, when an SR P2MP P-tunnel is not shared across EVIs, the label field is set to zero and the Tree-SID is sufficient to identify the EVI. When it is shared across two or more EVIs, the label field MUST contain an upstream-assigned label or one from a global context that the advertising PE has bound to the EVI, and the ingress PE MUST impose it before the label representing the Tree-SID.

For SRv6, an EVI is identified by an SRv6 SID encoded in the Segment Routing Header of an IPv6-encapsulated packet, and this is required even if the tree is not shared. The advertising ingress PE MUST attach a BGP Prefix-SID attribute to the IMET or S-PMSI auto-discovery routes with the SRv6 L2 Service TLV, and the SRv6 Endpoint behavior of the SID Information Sub-TLV SHOULD be END.DT2M. The SID MUST be the last segment in the segment list of the Segment Routing Header. An egress PE MUST NOT install the SRv6 SID in its forwarding table.

EVPN requires split-horizon filtering with Ethernet Segment multihoming, to prevent duplicate broadcast, unknown unicast or multicast traffic. In SR-MPLS, the procedures for P2MP label switched paths in Section 8.3.1.2 of RFC 7432 are sufficient. For a shared tree the ESI label sits at the bottom of the label stack, followed by an EVI context label, and the Tree-SID label of the tree instance is at the top.

For SRv6, the Arg.FE2 argument of the End.DT2M behavior is used for ESI-based split-horizon filtering. The ingress PE assigns it and it identifies an Ethernet Segment of origin, which is analogous to the upstream-assigned ESI MPLS label in RFC 7432. The ingress PE encodes it with the SRv6 SID in the Segment Routing Header by doing a bitwise logical OR operation, and the egress PE uses the Arg.FE2 to perform ESI-based split-horizon filtering.

EVPN with IR follows the same colored-route approach as MVPN, with the egress PE coloring its IMET route, and the ingress PE replicating the payload into the matching SR-TE policy. Support for the Inter-AS and Inter-Region segmentation procedures of RFC 9572 with SR P2MP P-tunnels is out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: Ethernet VPN uses the same two transport options, but its routes are named differently. EVPN also has to avoid sending the same broadcast back out of the door it came in through when a site is connected to two routers. In SR-MPLS this uses a label at the bottom of the stack; in SRv6 it uses a value carried in the segment identifier.

sections.title: IANA Code Points
sections.content:
IANA has assigned two values in the PMSI Tunnel Types registry (RFC 7385): 0x0C for SR-MPLS P2MP Tree and 0x0D for SRv6 P2MP Tree.

IANA has also allocated three code points in the SRv6 Endpoint Behaviors registry (RFC 8986): 76 (0x004C) for End.DTMC4, 77 (0x004D) for End.DTMC6 and 78 (0x004E) for End.DTMC46, each with IETF as the change controller.

These three behaviors are defined in Section 3.1. End.DTMC4 is functionally identical to End.DT4 except that the forwarding lookup MUST be performed in the IPv4 multicast routing table rather than the IPv4 unicast routing table, and it MUST only be associated with the SRv6 Multicast Service SID carried in AFI/SAFI 1/129 auto-discovery routes. End.DTMC6 does the same for the IPv6 multicast routing table and AFI/SAFI 2/129 routes. End.DTMC46 uses the IP multicast routing table and may be associated with either route type.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA has given the two new tunnel types and the three new Segment Routing over IPv6 endpoint behaviors their own code points, so that different implementations name the same thing the same way.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that the procedures it defines do not introduce any additional security considerations beyond those mentioned in RFC 6513, RFC 6514, RFC 7432 and RFC 9572. For the general security considerations applicable to SR P2MP Policy and Replication segments, it points to RFC 9960 and RFC 9524 respectively.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC adds no new security rules. The safety requirements of the earlier multicast and Ethernet VPN documents still apply, along with those for Segment Routing P2MP policies and replication segments.
